title: Whose are these? Kenen …?
focus: Ask whose one or several things are without adding a personal suffix.
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Choose “Whose pillows are these?” in Finnish. Use tyynyt (“pillows”), nämä ovat (“these are”).
exercises.explanation: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Whose questions with kenen: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: kenen + unsuffixed plural noun + nämä + ovat

parts.formation: Kenen is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”). Several things do not by themselves change kenen.
tyyny + -t = tyynyt. No personal owner is named, so keep -t and add no personal possessive suffix.
Nämä is the plural of tämä and identifies several things.
Use ovat with plural nämä; begin the owner question with kenen, without onko.

optionFeedback.Kenen tyynyt nämä ovat?: Correct: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
optionFeedback.Kenen tyynynsä nämä ovat?: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
optionFeedback.Kenen tyynyt nämä on?: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
optionFeedback.Kuka tyynyt nämä ovat?: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
